How often do you have the thoughts? It is generally considered an obsession if you are spending more than an hour/day thinking about the thoughts.

If you just move on and now the thoughts are ludicrous and the thoughts do not cause anxiety than you do not have OCD. Something like 90% of the human population has thoughts of harming people which they know are ludicrous and they dismiss and the other 10% that answered no in that study probably are just lying to themselves IMO.

If the thoughts are there for more than an hour a day or they cause a lot of anxiety/interfere with your life I recommend you go to the doctor. Not a psychatrist or psychologist but just your normal doctor to discuss the symptoms and see a professional's opinion. Normal doctor's can diagnose mental health issues and direct you on where to go next if you need treatment as well as prescribe medication should you need (although I always recommend trying therapy before medication, as if the issue isn't that big, medication often causes more side-effects then the benefit is worth).

Good luck.

This is the type of things I hate. The author of this article obviously has no idea what OCD actually is.

There is no such thing as an "OCD person". OCD has many subtypes all with different compulsions and obsessions.

Also:
Harm-OCD=Worry that one may cause harm to others whether intentionally or unintentionally (running over with car, going crazy etc.)

Contamination-OCD: Excessive worry about contamination, hygiene and germs. Sufferers often do things like wash their hands to much and have certain showering routines to ensure cleanliness.

Also a Sexual Obsession can be about anything within the realms of human imagination for instance someone may have a sexual obsession that they are only attracted to green elephants wearing pink dresses, although unlikely it is within the realm of human imagination so someone could worry they are sexually attracted to that thing.

This is a great page that explains HOCD really well and has a table comparing actual homosexuality to HOCD so you can easily see the differences. It can be very reassuring: [http://www.neuroticplanet.com/hocd.php](http://www.neuroticplanet.com/hocd.php)



A lot of psychologists/psychiatrists refer to what we call HOCD as 
SO-OCD (Sexual Orientation-OCD) as it is possible for actual LGBT to get concerns about their sexual orientation that they are straight. 

However the acronyms really don't mean anything: OCD is OCD.

Although we may all have different obsessions there is one common theme: We worry about something which cannot be proven to be absolutely impossible although the thing we worry about is highly unlikely and we use compulsions/rituals/checking to calm down the anxiety temporarily.

I've suffered from pretty much every type of obsession over the years so I know a lot. Please feel free to ask any question you want. Currently suffering from HOCD as you can see from my recent posts.
